assessment.body:
## Verdict

agent_supports: yes
daemon_capability: full
driver_capability: ready

## Reasoning

Many turns of file-tool work on one session. On 2.x every turn is the same shape — a user row, assistant steps with tool items, an idle row, and the plugin's Stop hook — so each turn must read working → ready on the SAME ses_… id, with no waiting (the per-cell config allows the file tools) and no drift: the session stays bound to the one service pid throughout (pid.go servicePIDFor).

## Spec choices

- Six turns, each start at least 1s after the previous ready (the record's rule for anchoring past a hook-ended turn; since #2120 no bounce is expected, and none is anchored).
- The work is deliberately small (three tiny files, a summary, a note, a glob listing), so the shared local model's context stays small.
caveats: Smaller than V1's 2-6 (six files and longer prompts): the brief keeps the shared Kolibri context small; the stress here is turns and tool steps, not context size.

sources.note: 2.x hook receiver: permission.asked holds waiting, session.execution.{succeeded,failed,interrupted} end the turn through HandleStopHook (#2108)
each assistant row's model.id is the step's ModelName; text items feed applyAssistantText (task-estimate scan)
servicePIDFor: a session no client runs binds to the one running service; OwnsSharedPID answers false for an archived row

preconditions: One OpenCode 2.x `serve --service` running, with a model it can reach (this host: the sandbox service, local Kolibri-1 4-bit model (mlx_lm) at 127.0.0.1:8087); the rig never starts, stops or reconfigures it
The three XDG exports, coexist IRRLICHT_ONBOARD_HOME and a non-7837 bind address from replaydata/agents/opencode-v2/prerequisites.md; OPENCODE_DB unset
setup: driver-interactive.sh (API driver) refuses before creating anything unless exactly one `serve --service` runs, its environment carries the run's XDG_* values, and the plugin's beacon resolves this run's daemon

It creates one session over POST /api/session at <staging>/cwd, waits for the service log to show the plugin the daemon installed loading for that location with no load failure, then drives the script; the session's session_message rows are exported read-only as the transcript
settings allow the edit and read tools and deny the shell in RUN_CWD/opencode.json, so no permission ask can hold a file-tool turn

script.text: Using your write tool, create three files: step1.txt containing 1, step2.txt containing 2 and step3.txt containing 3. Do not ask me anything. Then reply with exactly: created
Using your read tool, read step1.txt, step2.txt and step3.txt back and tell me the number each one contains. Then reply with exactly: read-back-done
Using your write tool, create summary.md listing step1.txt 1, step2.txt 2 and step3.txt 3, one per line. Then reply with exactly: summary-written
Using your edit tool, append a new line total=6 to summary.md, then read summary.md back and show me its full contents. Then reply with exactly: total-appended
Using your write tool, create notes1.txt containing a single line: notes1. Then read it back. Then reply with exactly: notes-done
Using your glob tool, list the .txt and .md files in the current directory and tell me how many there are. Then reply with exactly: all-done

verify: six working → ready arcs on one ses_… session, each ended by its own Stop hook
one pid binding for the whole session
